plan.title: Answers the day-3 check-in once, then goes quiet: two daily texts, a second check-in, then silence

context.text: Hey Maya! Ten pages of Dune on the couch at 7 tonight. Ready?
Maya, two nights slipped. Forget the ten: just open Dune tonight and read one page. What's getting in the way?

transcript.text: Hey Maya. You said you wanted to read Dune every day, and you committed to it. Is that still true? If you don't want to do this anymore, just tell me and that's totally fine. If you do, let's do it: 10 pages on the couch at 7. And if the plan isn't working, we can change it to something that fits your life better. Let's just not give up on it.

Hey Maya! The last few days got away from us, but that's behind us. It's 7 in five minutes, so grab Dune and sit on the couch. Ten pages, then send me a photo of the page you stop on. Are you in for tonight?

Hey Maya, no guilt, let's just make tonight easy. Today is only five pages of Dune on the couch at 7, about 10 minutes, then a photo of the page you stop on. If something's been getting in the way this week, tell me what it is. Does five pages work for you?

Hey Maya, let's shrink tonight to almost nothing. Three pages of Dune on the couch at 7, about 5 minutes, then a photo of the page you stop on. You committed to this, and three pages is a start I know you can pull off. Can you do that for me?

Maya, I'd rather ask you straight than keep pushing. Do you still want Dune in your days? If you do, tonight is only 3 pages on the couch at 7, about 5 minutes, then a photo of the page you stop on. If the plan itself is what's not fitting your life, tell me and we'll reshape it. Which is it?

conversation.reason: One text per day at 6:50 with new angles (five pages, three pages), a reworded day-3 check-in with the real choice, and no text after it; the 6:55 reply runs longer than 'brief'.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression well: it sent the day-3 check-in, sent one text per day with a fresh angle each time, and reworded the third check-in while keeping the real choice. Its main weaknesses are wordy replies that go past three sentences and a final check-in that asks two questions.
